title: The 5 Oldest Cave Paintings Ever Found, Ranked (France Isn't on It)

scenes.text: The five oldest cave paintings ever found. France doesn't make the list.
Number five: El Castillo, Spain. A red disk at least forty thousand eight hundred years old.
scenes.label: El Castillo · 40,800 years

scenes.text: Number four: a life-size wild pig on Sulawesi, Indonesia. At least forty-five thousand five hundred years.
scenes.label: Sulawesi pig · 45,500 years

scenes.text: Number three: a pig with three human-like figures, also on Sulawesi. Fifty-one thousand two hundred years.
scenes.label: Pig and hunters · 51,200 years

scenes.text: Number two: hand stencils in Spanish caves, over sixty-four thousand years. Too old for modern humans, so likely Neanderthals.
scenes.label: Spanish caves · 64,000 years

scenes.text: Number one: a hand stencil on Muna island, Indonesia. At least sixty-seven thousand eight hundred years, fingertips reshaped into points. Lascaux in France? About seventeen thousand.
scenes.label: Muna stencil · 67,800 years

description:
The five oldest cave paintings ever dated, ranked by their minimum age.
A red disk in El Castillo cave, Spain, is at least 40,800 years old; a life-size warty pig in Leang Tedongnge on Sulawesi dates to at least 45,500 years; a pig with three human-like figures in Leang Karampuang, also on Sulawesi, is at least 51,200 years old; hand stencils and markings in Spanish caves such as Maltravieso are over 64,000 years old, before modern humans reached Europe, so likely made by Neanderthals; and a hand stencil with reshaped, pointed fingertips on Muna island, Indonesia, is at least 67,800 years old. Famous Lascaux is about 17,000 years old.
Which one surprised you most?
first_comment: Which would you put at number one? These are minimum ages, so any of them could turn out older. Bonus: the Muna stencil's fingers were reshaped to look pointed, maybe like an animal claw. What should we rank next?
